interface.signature: def longestSubstring(N: int, S: str) -> str:

preconditions.description: The input integer N must be within the range 1 to 1000 (inclusive), representing the length of the string S.
The string S must have exactly N characters.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(c, str) and len(c) == 1 for c in S)
preconditions.description: The string S must consist of exactly N single-character strings (i.e., no empty or multi-character elements).

postconditions.description: The function returns either -1 (indicating no repeating non-overlapping substring exists) or a non-empty string representing the longest repeating non-overlapping substring.

postconditions.expression: return_value != -1 and all(S.count(return_value) >= 2 for _ in range(2))
postconditions.description: If the function returns a substring, it must appear at least twice in S without overlapping (i.e., the two occurrences do not share any character positions).

postconditions.expression: return_value == -1 or (all(len(return_value) >= len(candidate) for candidate in [sub for sub in [S[i:j] for i in range(N) for j in range(i+1, N+1)] if S.count(sub) >= 2 and not any(S.find(sub) == k and S.find(sub, k+1) < k+len(sub) for k in range(N-len(sub)+1))]))
postconditions.description: The returned substring (if not -1) must be the longest possible substring that appears at least twice in S without overlapping. If multiple such substrings exist, the one that appears first in S (i.e., has the earliest starting index) is chosen.
